reviews.comment: The best I've had the pleasure of taking at A&M; he has a lot of wisdom to share. The thought-provoking discussion sections involve unpacking ~2 films and journals a week, with some additional short assigned and in-class writings, and one final paper. As long as you're showing up, putting in the work, and thinking critically, you'll earn an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Get ready to read! He will have you buy at minimum six novels, and if you want to remotely do well in the class you will have to read them. He grades by very few things and he is a HARD grader. He will curve if he has to, and he says the answers are relative, but he is actually looking for answers specific to him. 4 writing assignments & 2 exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think people should know he is a HARD GRADER and, a bit unfair. I sit behind his class and pay attention but he makes it so hard to succeed because, of his lack of support as a professor. TELL me which English class have you memorized the dates of freaking poems for the test (midterms) and, the authors? It's not a history class but English.

I loved Dr. Alonzo's class! I had him for my Senior Seminar: Chicanx Literature. The readings were lengthy but were very interesting and I was introduced to a multitude of writers, two of which I will now be reading more frequently. You definitely have to put in the work and participate frequently! Great professor and cares about his students.

Since being enrolled in his Film course until now, a decade later, Dr. Alonzo remains someone who has positively influenced my film career in one way or another. This class allowed me to freely express contemplative creative thought about film. I may not have known then just how much of an impact he'd have on me, but now I am forever grateful.

He is a great lecturer and always kept the evening classes entertaining. He does call on students in lecture though, so make sure you read the assigned readings and come ready to ask a question. However the readings weren't that bad for an ENGL class and he only required two discussion posts a week in regards to homework. 10/10, he really cares.

Nice person, but hes really difficult. Lots of reading/ lots of disc board stuff/lots of hw. Dont use any outside sources or hell threaten to flag you & then give u a blown out of proportion situation w honors office. Dont take unless you genuinely enjoy reading 200+ pgs for hw. Save yourself the mental/ physical stress just take a diff class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Alonzo is a wonderful professor. He can be a bit unorganized sometimes but he still manages to help us learn about the books we are reading in class and provides historical contexts for the books that we are reading. Very easy going english professor
